bounded_question: What are the serializer 0x60ba600's 25 per-kind rules -- the single documented boundary of #3485 -- and how does each rule turn a Find-pipeline value into its text form, end to end including the decimal, escape, hex, double and enum-name helpers?

kind_rules.rule: bool: byte at *value, nonzero -> "true" (0x43f883), zero -> "false" (0x430e89); _M_replace into out.
i32 at *value -> signed decimal via int_to_string 0x5f06bb0, then move_assign into out.
i32 at *value -> same helper, same value; behaviorally identical to kind 1.
i64 at *value -> signed decimal: absolute value, '-' fill, two-digit table loop; INT64_MIN -> "-9223372036854775808".
u32 at *value -> unsigned decimal, 32-bit divide-by-100 loop, two-digit table.
u8 at *value -> signed decimal via int_to_string 0x5f06bb0 (zero-extended byte).
u32 at *value -> unsigned decimal, second copy of the kind-4 loop (separate code, same behaviour).
u64 at *value -> unsigned decimal, 64-bit divide-by-100 loop, two-digit table.
u64 at *value -> unsigned decimal, second copy of the kind-7 loop (separate code, same behaviour).
(ptr, len) at *value -> backslash-escaped copy via escape_copy 0x61d0f30, then move_assign into out.
f64 at *value -> "%f" via snprintf_string 0x60ba450 (vsnprintf, 328-byte buffer), then move_assign into out.
u8 enum name: linear walk of the head list at map 0x65070a0 + 0x10 (node next +0x00, name +0x08, key +0x28); on match _M_assign the name into out; on miss return 0.

u8 enum name, map 0x6507160; same walk as kind 11.

open_unknowns: Kinds 1 and 2 are behaviorally identical (both call int_to_string 0x5f06bb0 with the same 32-bit value), as are kinds 4/6 (u32) and 7/8 (u64); the binary gives no gloss for which C++ types the duplicated kinds stand for, so the model records the duplication faithfully and does not name the types.

The seven enum maps live in .bss (runtime-built); the model takes them as harness-injected EnumMap objects, not binary reads. The serializer's enum walk is a plain head-list walk, unlike the hash-bucket walk the #3560 parsers use in the other direction.

The double kind formats with C %f via vsnprintf; Python '%f' matches it on ordinary values, inf and nan. A negative NaN's sign is not pinned (the binary's vsnprintf would print '-nan'; the model does not special-case it).

The serializer's value struct layout beyond the per-kind reads is not pinned: each kind reads only the bytes its rule needs (1, 4 or 8 bytes at *value, or a 16-byte (ptr, len) pair for kinds 9 and 23).
Which construction paths install a non-null +0x28 delegate (carried from #3485) is still not pinned.
The global default name at 0x6508980 and the delegate vtable base (carried from #3485/#3560) are still not pinned.

0x5f06bb0.name: int_to_string
0x5f06bb0.role: Signed i32 decimal (std::to_string(int)): sign bit, absolute value, magnitude thresholds, '-' fill, two-digit table loop; INT32_MIN formats as '-2147483648'.

0x60b79e0.name: move_assign
0x60b79e0.role: String move-assign: moves the source string into the destination (re-shipped byte-identical from #3488).

0x60ba450.name: snprintf_string
0x60ba450.role: vsnprintf into a string: calls the function pointer in GOT 0x64ed730 (vsnprintf) with a 328-byte stack buffer, then installs the result in the out string (SSO or _M_create + memcpy).

0x60ba600.name: serializer
0x60ba600.role: Value serializer: dispatches on kind (jump table 0x978650, 25 entries, 19 targets) and writes the value's text form into the out string; returns 1 on success, 0 with out untouched for kinds 0x11..0x16 and kind > 0x18. Sole direct caller is the matcher 0x60bb9a0 (site 0x60bbb97).

0x61c7e30.name: hex_encode
0x61c7e30.role: Hex encode / raw copy: flag 1 reserves 2*len and writes two UPPERCASE hex chars per byte via hexchar; flag 0 replaces out with the raw input bytes. The serializer always passes flag 1.

0x61d0e90.name: escape_predicate
0x61d0e90.role: Needs-escape test: true for 0x0a, 0x0d, '#' (0x23), ':' (0x3a) and '\\' (0x5c) only; the bit-test mask is 0x0200000000800001 (bits {0, 23, 57} over byte - 0x23); bytes above 0x5c return 0.

0x61d0f00.name: escape_letter
0x61d0f00.role: Escape letter: 0x0a -> 'n', 0x0d -> 'r', anything else -> the byte itself.

0x61d0f1c.name: escape_copy_cleanup
0x61d0f1c.role: Escape-copy landing pad: disposes the out string, then _Unwind_Resume.

0x61d0f30.name: escape_copy
0x61d0f30.role: Backslash-escape copy: for each input byte, escape_predicate decides; escaped bytes become '\\' + escape_letter, the rest are copied raw. The inverse of the escape decoder 0x61d0ee0 pinned by #3560.
